full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah, J:- These 5 (five) criminal appeals and the two rules 
aving arisen out of the same judgment and order dated 12.8.2002 passed by the learned Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong in Sessions Trial Case No. 82 of 2000, were heard together and are being deposed of by this single judgment. 

2. By the impugned judgment and order the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong found Osman 0 Md. Osman @ Osmannya, Ali Akbar @ Didarul @ Didar, Zillur Rahman @ Zillur, Zahid Hossain Kiron and Md. Siddidue guilty of the charges levelled against them tinder section 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced each of them to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of taka 5,000/- (five thousand) each, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for I (one) year more each and acquitted accused Yeasin Rahman @ Rahman Yeasin @ Titu from the charges leveled against him tinder section 302/109 of the Penal Code, Alamgir and Omar All @ Jahangir @ Jahangir Kashai from the charges brought against them under section 302/34 of the Penal Code. The learned Sessions Judge acquitted all the accused from the charges leveled against them under section 120B of the Penal Code. 

3. Government Criminal Appeal No.28 of 2002 has been filed by the state against the order sentencing the convicts, namely, Osman @ Md. Osman @ Osmainnaya, Ali Akbar Didanil Alam @ Didar, Zillur Rahman @ Zillur, Zahid Hossain Kiron and Md. Siddque to suffer imprisonment for life instead of awarding capital sentence against them. 

4. Government Criminal Appeal No.34 of 2002 has been filed against the order acquitting Yeasin Rahman @ Rahman Yeasin @, Titu, of the charges brought against him under sections 302/109 and 120B of the Penal code 120B of the penal code and alamgir and Osman from the charges leveled against them under section 302/34 and 120B of the Penal Code. 

5. Criminal appeal No-3023 of 2002 has been filed by convict Zillur Rahman. 

6. Criminal Appeal No. 2971 of 2002 has been filed by convicts All Akbar @ Didar, Zahid Hossain @ Kiran and Md. Siddique. 

7. Criminal Appeal No. 2981 of 2002 has been filed by convict Osman @ Md. Osman @ Osmannya. 

8. The initial prosecution case as stated by p.w.l, James Roy, the informant, in short,' was that deceased Jibran Tayyabi was the agency manager of Centras Maritime (BD) of which he was an employee, their office being at 69, Agrabad commercial area, Chittagong. The occurrence took place on 9.6.99. On the said date at about 5.30 p.m. Jibran Taiyyabi went out of the office in his own Car being Chattra Metro-ga- 11-1093 for his residence. Jibran himself was driving the car and when he reached at the middle place of Band box laundry and Chung king Restaurant at Sheikh Mujib Road, Agrabad, Chittagong, some one stopped his car and shot at him and then some one took him to Chittagong Medical College Hospital (hereinafter referred to as the hospital) in the said car. After Jibran Tayyabi was taken to hospital doctor there declared him dead. When the informant reached his residence at 8-10 p.m. he came to know that a person from his office informed over telephone that some one killed Jibran Tayyabi. Immediately after hearing the said information the informant went to the hospital and in the emergency ward saw Jibran dead. Jibran used to live at 5/6, Zakir Hossain Road with his wife Titli. On the next day the informant after drafting a First Information Report (FIR) went to the police station and lodged the same with Double Mooring police station. 

9. After investigation police submitted charge sheet in the case on 22.11.99 against as many as 8 persons including the convict-appellants under sections 302/109/120B/34 of the Penal Code. All the accused including the absconding accused, namely, Yasin: Rahman Tim and Md. Alamgir were put on 7 trial before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong. All the accused except Yasin Rahman @ Titu were charged under sections 302/34 and 120B of the Penal Code. Absconding, accused Yasin Rahman @ Titu was charged separately under section 302/109 and 120B of the Penal Code, The charges being read over to the accused present they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

10. To substantiate the charges against the accused the prosecution produced as many as 49 witnesses; of them P.ws.11, 12 and 15 and were tendered and p.w.16 was declared hostile. 

11. The absconding accused were defended by the state defence lawyer. 

12. The defence did not examine any witness, but cross-examined the prosecution witnesses except p.w.15. The defence case as it appeared from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses was that the deceased was killed by P.Ws 3, 4 and 10 along with others somewhere else and then they in order to conceal their said act boarded the dead body in a car, and by keeping the car behind a truck took the dead body to hospital to make it a case of accident. Further defence case was that one Rony Khan who was a divorcee at the time of the occurrence developed love affairs with Titli, wife of the deceased and it is he got the deceased killed by the hired killers. It was also the defence case that deceased Jibran was involved with international smuggling group and out of enmity over the booty he was killed by the smugglers. Besides the above defence the common defence taken by all the accused was that they were not involved with the killing of the accused but were implicated in the case falsely by extracting confessional statements from some of the accused through torture. 

13. On conclusion of the trial the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by the impugned judgment and order, found the appellants of Criminal appeals No.3023 of 2002, 2971 of 2002 and 2981 of 2002 guilty of the charges brought, against them under section 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced each of them to suffer imprisonment as already stated at the very outset of the judgment and acquitted the other accused from the respective charges leveled against them. 

14. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of  conviction and sentence the convicts preferred the criminal appeals as mentioned above and the State filed Government Criminal Appeal No. 34 of the 2002 against the order of acquittal of the accused, namely, Yasin Rahman @ Rahman Yasin @ Titu, Alamgir and Omar Ali (wrongly , written as Osman Ali @ Jahangir @ Jahingir Kasai from the charges brought against them. Government also filed Criminal Appeal No.28 of 2002 against the sentence passed by the learned Sessions against the said convict appellants. 

15. Mr. Momtaz Uddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr. Saifuddin Ahmed Chowdhury in Criminal Appeal No. 3023 of 2002 submitted that the prosecution totally failed to prove any fact as to the involvement of appellant Zillur Rahman with the killing of deceased Jibran Tayyabi in any manlier whatsoever; the only incriminating material against the appellant is the confessional statement allegedly made by him but the same not being true and voluntary and having been obtained by torturing him both physically and mentally and producing him from police custody could not be the basis of his conviction, but the learned Sessions Judge failed to consider the said legal aspect of the case in passing the impugned judgment and order. Mr. Momtazuddin Ahmed further submitted that the confessional statement allegedly made by accused Zillur Rahman was not recorded in compliance with the provisions of section 164 read with section 364 of the Code of Criminal procedure (the Code), therefore, the same could not be treated as true and voluntary, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge acted illegally in relying upon the same in finding the appellant guilty of the charges leveled against him. Mr. Ahmed further submitted that Zillur Rahman was a student leader of Chhatra Dal and while Police Inspector Delwar Hossein was posted at Patia police station he used to protest his illegal activities and said Delwar (p.w.47) also believed that Zillur Rahman was responsible for his transfer from the said police and he out of the said grudge by influencing the detective branch of the police involved him (Zillur Rahman) in the case by extracting confession from him and during cross examination though the defence gave categorical suggestion to p.w. 47 to the said effect, yet the learned Sessions Judge did not consider the said fact and thus erred in law in arriving at the finding of guilt against the appellant of the charges leveled against him. Mr. Momtaz Uddin Ahmed lastly submitted that Aleya Begum (p.w.5) in whose residence the accused persons allegedly assembled before killing the deceased mentioned the name of Osman only and p.ws.18, 20-35 also did not mention the name Zillur Rahman, therefore, the prosecution failed to prove the fact of his presence either at the residence of said Aleya Begum or at the place where Jibran was shot, he is entitled to be acquitted of the charges leveled against him. 

16. Mr. Sharfuddin Khan Mukul, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants in Criminal Appeal No.2971 of 2002 as well as in the government appeals for the said respondents submitted that the learned Sessions Judge acted illegally in finding the appellants guilty of the charges leveled against them under section 302/34 of the Penal Code inasmuch as the prosecution failed to prove-beyond all reasonable doubt the time, place and the manner of the occurrence. He further submitted that no alamat having been seized from the broken car and from the alleged place of the occurrence prima-facie showed that the deceased was not shot at the place as claimed by the prosecution. He further submitted that the confessional statements made by the accused do not tally with the postmortem report in that in the post mortem report it was specifically mentioned that gun shot pierced towards the Jeff side of the back of the chest whereas, in the confessional statement of the accused it was stated that the deceased Was shot by breaking the glass of the right side of the car and the said anomaly creates clear doubt about the 
manner of the alleged occurrence as claimed by the prosecution, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge ought to have disbelieved the entire prosecution case. Mr. Mukul further submitted that the confessional statements of the accused and the evidence of p.w. 5 Aleya Begum and P.w.I9 Liakat being contradictory to each other those could not be accepted as true and voluntary and so no reliance could be put upon the same and consequently it cannot he hold that it is the appellants who killed deceased; Jihran Tayyabi. Mr. Sharfuddin also made similar submissions in respect of the evidentiary value of the confessional statements of the accused as made by Mr. Momtazuddin Ahmed in considering the guilt of the appellants of the charges brought against them. Mr. Sharfuddin lastly submitted that p.w.5 Aleya Begum did not identify the accused persons in the dock and p.w. 16 did not support the prosecution case for which he was declared hostile and their learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge himself having disbelieved the prosecution Case of criminal conspiracy to kill the deceased he ought to have acquitted the appellants as criminal conspiracy being the whole basis of the case of the prosecution the appellant could not be connected otherwise with the killing of the deceased and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. Mr. Rokan Uddin Mahmood the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Yeasin Rahman @ Rahman Yeasin @ Titu in. Government Criminal Appeal No.34 of 2002 submitted that accused Yeasin was no where in the alleged conspiracy and planning in killing deceased Tayyabi to remove the hurdle to get his fiance as alleged by the, prosecution through p.ws.32 and 48, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge rightly acquitted him. He further submitted that the prosecution totally tailed to adduce any evidence to show that any payment was made to the confessing accused or Osman as the booty to kill the deceased as claimed by p.w.48 or any other fact to show the alleged conspiracy out of the jealousy which grew between Tim and Jibran centering Samanja, the question of proof of the charges leveled against the said respondent under section 302/109 and 1208 of the Penal Code does not arise at all and, as such, no interference is called for with the impugned order of acquittal passed against him. 

17. Mr. Abdur Razzaque Khan, the learned Additional Attorney General appearing for the state in Government Criminal Appeals No. 28 of 2002 and 34 of 2002 as well as in the criminal appeals filed by the convicts submitted that the instant case is peculiar in its nature and cannot be dealt with like any other ordinary case of killing as we generally come across. He further submitted that the instant case was a clear case of conspiracy of very unique and smart in nature of which the master player was Yeasin Rahman @ Titu and if the entire circumstances of the case, the confessional statements of the other co-accused are considered along with the evidence of p.ws.5 and 19 as a whole but not in isolation it would appear that the prosecution proved the charges leveled against all the accused beyond all reasonable doubt so they all were liable to be sentenced to death. Mr. Khan further, submitted that p.w.2 having categorically deposed that he was present at the place of the occurrence and he saw the occurrence and heard the sound of 2(two) firing shots and p.ws 3, 4 and 10 also having categorically deposed that they on seeing rush of the people in front of Chung king Chinese restaurant went there and saw Jibran Tayyabi in injured condition in the car, the prosecution proved the place of the occurrence as well as the manner of the occurrence. Mr. Khan further submitted that in considering the charge of criminal conspiracy to kill Jibran, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge totally failed to consider the break down of the telephone calls of mobile telephone No. 017750895 and 018311175 which prima-facie proved that it is Yasin Rahman Titu who supervised the entire plan of killing of deceased Jibran through accused Alamgir keeping himself away from the actual place of the occurrence, so he along with all the other co-accused were very much involved with the criminal conspiracy for killing Jibran Taiyyabi within the meaning of section 120B of the Penal Code and q11 ought to have been found guilty of the charges leveled against them Under the said section. Mr. Khan further submitted that when the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge believed the case of the prosecution that accused Zillur Rahman, Didar, Osman, Kiron and Siddique were involved with the killing of the deceased he ought to have believed the prosecution case that they all did the job as a part of the conspiracy as hired killers masterminded by Titu otherwise the said accused had no reason to kill the deceased. Mr. Khan also submitted that immediately after the occurrence Yeasin Rahman @ Thu. absconded and though steps, were taken to secure his arrest, yet he could not he arrested and in fact he fled away from the country which clearly showed that he was very much involved with the criminal conspiracy of killing Jibran and got the conspiracy implemented by the other accused. Mr. Khan lastly submitted that
immediately after the occurrence Ali Akbar Didarul Alam @ Didar and Osman went to India using fake passports which facts also lend support to the prosecution case of criminal conspiracy and, as such, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge acted illegally in acquitting the accused from the charges leveled against them under section 1208 of the Penal Code and, therefore, the government appeals should be allowed and all the accused be sentenced to death. 

18. Let us now see the evidence on record as adduced by the prosecution. 

19. P.W.1 is the informant and he deposed to the same effect as already stated while stating the initial case of the prosecution, so, we do not repeat the testimony of p.w.1 again here. He proved the FIR lodged by him as exhibit I and his signature therein as exhibit 1 /1. In cross-examination by the defence this p.w. stated that Jibran Tayyabi was an Indian national and he used to work in Bangladesh legally. On getting an information at 8.10 p.m. he went to the hospital and found the police officers along with others, present at the emergency ward but he did not talk to any one. He did not inform the Chairman of the company before lodging the F.I.R. which was lodged by him on the next day at 10.55 hours. He could not say as to whether the wife of Jibran had gone to the hospital. He used to attend the office by the road passing in front of Chung King restaurant. There were many shops below Chung king restaurant. The p.w. further stated that before lodging the F.I.R he inquired from the duty officer as to whether any other F.I.R was lodged; but he could not .remember his name. Wife of Jibran used to serve in Chittagong Grammar School. On the date of the occurrence after Jibran left the office he remained in the offence for 10/15 minutes. He further stated that he remained in the hospital for 5 minutes then went to the house of the office assistant and remained there up to 12/I o'clock. He saw the place of the occurrence on the next day from the car while going to the office but he did not see any mark of blood. He did not inquire who took Jibran to the hospital. There were two women employees in their office out of 7 (seven), and the name of one of the employees was Rahima. He went to the hospital at 9 p.m. He lodged the FAR after hearing about the occurrence, but he himself saw the dead Body. He pleaded ignorance as to whether before 12 (twelve) hours of the lodging of the F.I.R by him police seized some alamats. He denied the defence suggestion that they after discussing the matter throughout the whole night filed the case in a preplanned way to suppress the actual facts and that Jibran was not shot at the time, place and in the manner as alleged. 

20. On recall the p.w. deposed that on 28.06.1999 he filed an application before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Chittagong for taking Toyota Sidan Private Car No. Chattra Metro Ga- 11-1093 which was owned by their company. Centras Maritime Limited in his `jimma' and took the car in his 'jimma'. He further deposed that deceased Jibran Taiyyabi used to drive the seized car. He proved the jimma Nama' as exhibit 25 and his signature therein as exhibit 25/1. In further cross-examination the p.w. stated that the seized car was not brought to court. In the 'jimma nama' it was not stated from where the car was taken in the 'jimma'. 

21. P.W.2, Fazlul Hoque, was the owner of the laundry; named, Band Box which was at
Sheikh Mujib Road situated by the side of Chung King Restaurant. The p.w. stated in 4, his examination-in-chief that the occurrence took place on 9.6.99, it about 5/5.15. He was present at the place of the occurrence and he saw the same. He came to his laundry at 4 p.m. on the date of the occurrence. At the time of the occurrence while a white car coming from the south reached in front of his shop a red Honda came with an accused and after stopping the said Honda in front of the car two persons stood by the two sides of 4 the car and 4 (four) others stood in front of the car with arms and then after breaking the glass of the door two persons remained standing. Jibran was sitting in the driving seat of the car. The p.w. heard the sound of two firing shots and found the man sitting in the car being shot and then the car after moving slowly stopped behind a truck. They got scared and people started coming at the place of the occurrence. Subsequently he heard that the car was taken to medical. He was examined by the police and his statements were recorded. In cross-examination the p.w. denied all the defence suggestions put to him to the effect that whatever he said in his examination-in-chief about the witnessing of the occurrence he did not say so to the investigation officer. He that he had been doing his business in the area for the last 15/16 years. He did not see whether blood of the victim poured at the place of the occurrence. He also could not say whether the broken glass of the car fell on the road. He further stated that he was in the shop sip to 9 p.m. Police came. subsequently. He could not say whether after the occurrence police seized any alamat from the place of the occurrence. He could not say when the police came. The p.w. denied the further defence suggestion that the police did not come at the place where the car was first stopped. He could not remember whether Kamal (p.w.10), Murad (p.w.4), Alamgir (p.w.3) brought the dead body in a car and then keeping the same just behind a truck shouted saying "accident accident". He pleaded his ignorance as to whether those 3 (three) persons took the dead body to the hospital and subsequently absconded. Police came to the place of the occurrence after they came to know that the deceased was an important man. He also denied the defence suggestion that he went into hiding and remained so for more than 2 (two) months. He stated that he gave statements to the investigation officer Rader Khan in his shop on 12.08.99. but he could not remember whether he gave statements to any other investigation officer. He further asserted that at the time of the occurrence he was in his shop and did not see to shot. He could not remember whether he stated to the investigating, officer that he saw to break the door of the car by stone. He denied the defence suggestion that no occurrence took place at the time and at the place as stated by him. 

22. P.W.3 is one Alamgir Hossain @ Joy. He deposed that previously he used to work in the show room of Metro Car Center which was situated at Sheikh Mujib Road. The occurrence took place on 9.6.99 at about 5.30 p.m, being Wednesday. He knew the place of the occurrence. He came to his said center after taking lunch at 2.30 o'clock. As he had no work in his hand he was sleeping in a Micro Bus. At about 5/5-30 p.m. Shahid a peon of the shop woke him up by pushing shouting that something happened on the other side of the road. Then he rushed to the place of the occurrence and saw the glass of all the 3 (three) sides being right, left and front of a white car broken and a man sitting in the drive seat leaning his face towards the west. He also found Kamal and Hasan Murad standing. The said 2 (two) who were known to him from before told him to drive the car as he knew the driving so that the life of the man could be saved. At that time the right side door of the driving seat was open and they shifted the man at the back seat of the car from the front seat by the said door and Kamal and Hasan also sat at the back seat with the said Injured man and he sitting in the driving seat drove the car to the hospital. The p.w. further deposed that he along with the said 2 and some medical staff took the man to the emergency ward of the hospital and then, they went to the 3rd floor, where the doctor told them about the necessity of blood and while they were looking for the blood one man came and informed that the man, died and thereafter they brought the dead body down. In the meantime Hasan Murad by bringing out a card from the pocket of the said dead man telephoned some where after 15/20 minutes a car came from where a woman and a man got down and when Kamal asked the driver of the car who was the woman driver replied that she was the wife of the person who died. Then they told the said woman that they tried to save the man but failed. He further stated that they, gave the woman the key of the car, briefcase and the other things which they found, with the deceased. They also gave the car to the woman and heard from her that the name of the dead person was Jibran. Thereafter, they went to their respective places of working by a taxi. The pm. further stated that subsequently he heard that the terrorist killed the man by shooting. Police examined him at his place of working after one month from the date of the occurrence. He further assented that he deposed in court what he told 
to the police. In cross-examination by the defence he asserted that after the occurrence t he, Kamal and Hasan did not go into hiding. He could not remember whether he made statements to the investigation officer on 30.799. He denied the defence suggestion that it was not correct that he did not tell to the investigating officer about the fact of handing over the car. He further stated that the medical staff took the man to the lift in a stretcher. He denied the defence suggestion that he used to earn his livelihood by committing dacoity theft and car hijacking, and he never worked at the Metro car center. He asserted that on the next day of the occurrence he was in the show room and he did not take any leave. He denied the further defence suggestion that Masud and Zakir were also with them. He further stated that he could not remember as to whether he saw any broken glass on the road. He also did not mark whether there was any broken glass inside the car. He denied the further, defence suggestion that they after killing Jibran by their own men somewhere else took the dead body to the hospital by staging a drama of accident keeping the car behind the truck. He denied the further defence suggestion's that after giving the things to Rony Khan their known man they fled away. 

23. P.W.4, Hasan Murad was one amongst the 3(three) who took the deceased to hospital. He deposed to the same effect as deposed by p.w.3 about the fact of going to the place of the occurence, seeing the deceased in the car and taking him to the hospital. He further deposed that when Alamgir (p.w.3) and Kamal (p.w.10) ran for blood for the injured, he in order to find his address searched the pocket and found a money bag and from there found a card but the same being written in English he could not read the same; he after getting the same read by a boy present at the place found the name as Jiban and then telephoned him. The person who received the telephone told that there was no Jibon but there was some one as Jibran, then he told him that Jibran was in the hospital being sick. He further deposed that when the man on the other end asked his name he identified him as sumon. Thereafter he went to the 3rd floor and when met Alamgir and Kamal they told him that the man died, In cross-examination by the defence similar questions having been put as were put to p.w.3 this p.w. answered in the similar manner The defence also gave similar suggestions to this p.w. as were given to p.w.3 and he gave similar answer, so, we do not repeat what he stated in his cross examination. 

24. P.W.5 is Aleya Begum, wife of Zahid Hossain. She stated in her examination in chief that previously she used to stay at Eidgah Pur and presently she was at Mistri Para. She was a house wife. She came to Chittagong at a tender age. She married 10 years before and had 2(two) sons. One and half year before her husband had to go to jail hajat in connection with a 'maramari' case. During the absence of her husband, she being in financial crisis, Saidul of Pannapara told her to start selling heroin which would give financial solvency to both of them and accordingly, he gave her 2/3 purias of heroin. Saidul told about his friend Liakat of Mistry Para. Liakat used to purchase heroin from her. Saidul used to supply her heroin. Along with Liakat his other friends also used to come and one day he introduced one Osman to her who also used to come with his friend after a gape of 4/5 days. Osman used to sit along with his friends in the vacant room by the side of her room. Lastly  one year before, being Wednesday (the date she could not remember) Osman came with his friends to her but she told him her, inability to sell heroin any more as her Jamider forbade her. But Osman having requested her for heroin in a very humble way she gave 3(three) purias which were with her as last stock and he purchased the same. She further stated that Osman had a ‘‘যন্ত্র” which sounded "কিউ কিউ" Osman by taking the 'যন্ত্র" near his ear told to the effect "আমি আসিতেছি” and then went away; when she demanded price for the heroin Osman pushed her by her neck. At that time it was about 5/5-10 p.m. She further stated that after half an hour Osman left she heard the sound of two firing shots near Chum King Restaurant. Subsequently she heard by the by that an Indian was shot in the car. She gave statements to the investigation officer as well as to the Magistrate. She proved her left thumb impression in the statements made by her under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the code). The p.w. identified Osman in court and asserted that he was indebted to her taka 1,100/00. In cross-examination she stated that she gave statements to the police after two months from the date of hearing of the sound. She would not be able to state the name of 2/1 persons who knew her and she did not know the ward commissioner of her area. She after denying the defence suggestion that to the police she told the name of her husband Jahid Hossain asserted that to the police she stated the name of her husband as Zahidur Rahnian. She also asserted that to the police she gave her address being the house of Yousuf Shaudagar, Mistri Para and denied the further defence suggestion that she did not give any specific address of her before the Magistrate. She further asserted that she was at the said house till she gave statements to the police. She further stated that she could not remember whether she told the police that she went on hiding after the occurrence was published in the newspaper. She denied the further defence suggestion that she did not tell the name of Liakat to the investigation officer and she also did not tell to the police that Liakat along with his friends used to come to her for purchasing heroin. She also denied the defence suggestion that what she stated in court about Osman she did not say so to the investigating officer and she never stayed at Mistri Para and she being involved in illegal and unsocial activities deposed falsely at they instance of the police on the assurance that she would be let off from those activities. 

25. P.W.6 is Aleya Begum @ Alo, wife of Ahmed Mia. She stated in her examination-in-chief that presently she was, staying at the house of Furkan Ali of Bagh Kunar 'মোড়’ prior to that she used to live at the house of Mofiz Khalifa of Lalkhan and before that she used to live at the house of Mr. Jainal at house No.7, Road No.5 Kulshi.  She was born in Calcutta. After her mother died in 1971 while she was aged about 3/4 years her father brought her to this country. In Bangladesh she first stayed at the house of her sister at Bias colony, Bahaddar Hat and thereafter started to work as a maid at the house of A.K. Khan where she worked for 5(five) years and then after his son Shamsuddin Khan @ Jambu Khan got separated from A. K. Khan she used to work as the 'Bua' in the house of Jambu Khan. While she had come to work in the house of A.K. Khan, Samanja, the daughter of Jambu Khan was aged about 1/11/2 years only. 2(two) years before she gave up the job of "Bua" the said house. 79. Before deciding the said questions let us first see whether deceased Jibran Tayyabi met natural death or was killed. To see this we can readily refer to two documentary evidence, namely, the inquest report (exhibit 4) and the postmortem report (exhibit 28). From a perusal of the said 2(two) documents it is prima-fade apparent that the deceased sustained bullet injuries. In the postmortem report 4 (four) lacerated wounds caused, by fire arm have been mentioned. The doctor opined that death was caused due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of the foe arm Injuries to the chest and right forearm which were anti mortem and homicidal in nature. Doctor who held the postmortem has been examined as p.w.40 and he deposed to the same effect. Besides the inquest report, the doctor's testimony and the postmortem report from the ocular testimony of p.ws. 1. 3, .4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 17, 21, 22 and 32 it appeared that p.ws.3, 4 and 10 took the deceased to the hospital being bullet hit where the doctors declared him dead and the other witnesses (p.w.s 1, 7, 8, 9, 17, 21, 22 and 32) who went to the hospital after hearing about the incident stated that they saw the dead body of Jibran in gory condition, so we hold that deceased Jibran did not meet a natural death but he was done to death by bullet injury. 
80. Now the next question is whether the deceased was shot at the middle place in between Band box and Chung King restaurant at the time and in the manner as alleged by the prosecution. 90. Criminal conspiracy has been defined in section 120 A of the Penal Code which is as under: " 
120A. Definition of Criminal conspiracy -when two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done:-
(1) an illegal act, or 
 (2) an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy: 
Provided that no agreement except an agreement to commit an offence shall amount to a criminal conspiracy unless some act besides the agreement is done by one or more parties to such agreement in pursuance thereof. 
Explanation- It is immaterial whether the illegal act is the ultimate object of such agreement, or is merely incidental to that object. 

A reading of Section 120A of the Penal Code shows that to constitute a criminal conspiracy there must he 2(two) elements one, two or more persons must agree to do or cause to do be done an illegal act and two, some act besides the agreement has to be done by one or more parties to such agreement in pursuance thereof. In the light of the definition of criminal conspiracy let as see whether there was an agreement between Yasin Rahman @ Titu and the other accused under the leadership of Osman to punish Jibran or to kill him for his relationship with Shamanja.

The evidence p.w. 33 shows that Titu monitored everything of the plan to kill Jibran over telephone with the help of Alamgir his cousin, the elder brother of Didar. The above facts also show how smartly and shrewdly every thing was planned to execute and implement the criminal conspiracy to kill Jibran. It is to be noted that in considering, the prosecution case of criminal conspiracy the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge totally failed to consider exhibit 16 and the evidence of p.w.33 

99. There is yet another strong circumstance in favour of the prosecution's case of criminal conspiracy to kill jibran which is that immediately after the occurrence accused Didar and Osman went on hiding and then went to India with fake passports as apparent from exhibits 17, 19, 20, 21, 33 and the ocular evidence of p.ws. 34, 35 and 44. Similarly accused Titu and Alamgir also went into hiding immediately after the occurrence and inspite of the fact that warrant of arrests and other legal processes were resorted to their arrest could not be, secured and the trial proceeded in their absence. So in view of the provisions of section 8 of the Evidence Act their involvement with the occurrence can very much be presumed. 

100. In this case there was some delay in lodging the F.I.R. and that too without giving the particulars of the occurrence, but in the facts and Circumstances of the case and the further fact that initially it was a case of clueless murder and a case of criminal conspiracy those factors cannot create any doubt on the whole prosecution case overthrowing the overwhelming evidence which ultimately surfaced during the course of investigation. There was also delay in examining the prosecution witnesses by the investigation officers but in the facts and circumstances of the instant case the delay in examining them cannot be treated as fatal to discard their testimony in court particularly of p.ws. 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14, 16, 20 and 32, their testimony being quite corroborative with the confessional statements of the accused; the reasons for our such view have been given while we discussed their evidence. 

101. In a case of criminal conspiracy it is not expected that the accused or the conspirator will enter into an agreement to do all illegal act by beating the drum. The conspiracy has to be found from the circumstances as well. In this case as discussed above, if the facts of the relationship of Shamanja with Titu and Jibran as came out from the testimony of p.w.6, the threat put by Titu to Jibran to leave Bangladesh as stated by p.w. 32, letter written by the then Assistant Indian High Commissioner to the Police Commissioner, Chittagong vide exhibit X-1, the testimony of p.ws. 7, 16 and 20, the confessional statements of the accused, the telephone break up of the telephone calls of two mobile telephones of Titu and Alamgir, the assembly of Osman and the other co-accused at the residence of Aleya (p.w.5) and their leaving of the residence of Aleya at 5/5-10 p.m., the absconsion of Titu and Alamgir after the occurrence and the going of Osman and Didar to India arc considered together a compact chain of very strong circumstance is established which any suggests as to the fact of a criminal reasonable doubt the charges levelled against each of the individual accused including the respondents of Government. Criminal Appeal No.34 of 2002 except accused Md. Siddique and they all are liable to be sentenced accordingly. 
However, considering the age of the acquitted accused and the further fact that the convicts already suffered part of their sentence, we are not inclined to sentence any of the accused to death.
